R0167.title: DAO Governance Attacks
R0167.definition: Attackers manipulating governance tokens or voting mechanisms to control decision-making power in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs).
R0167.description: DAOs make governance decisions through token voting. Attackers can manipulate voting results to pass malicious proposals (such as transferring funds, modifying contract parameters, granting themselves privileges) by buying or borrowing large amounts of governance tokens, using flash loans to temporarily gain voting power, bribing token holders, or exploiting proposal mechanism vulnerabilities.
R0167.influence: DAO funds are stolen or misused, governance mechanisms fail, community trust collapses.

observables: Governance token holdings spike concentratedly via flash loans or borrowing shortly before voting, then are returned immediately after voting
A voting proposal sees an anomalous surge of voting addresses near the deadline, with voting directions highly uniform
A new proposal requests fund transfers, contract parameter changes, or privilege grants, with the proposing address linked to whale addresses
Token holders receive organized bribes, with on-chain voting behavior correlated with bribe transactions
